plan: This is a second-price auction format where I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid. The dominant strategy in this format is to bid exactly my true value, since bidding higher risks overpaying (winning at a price above my value), and bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities without any benefit. My value is $9, so I should bid $9 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price auction where the winner pays the second-highest bid. In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value, regardless of what others do. Bidding my true value ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the market price (second-highest bid) and never overpay, while avoiding losses from bidding too high. With no prior history to inform deviations, truthful bidding is optimal.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (highest bid wins, pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value, regardless of what others do. Bidding higher than my value risks paying more than the item is worth to me if I win; bidding lower reduces my chance of winning without changing what I pay if I do win. Since my value is $34, I should bid $34 to maximize expected profit.
